For each matrix row apply a function over a ragged array

Source: R/matrix.R
tgs_matrix_tapply.Rd

For each matrix row (or column) apply a function to each cell of a ragged array, that is to each (non-empty) group of values given by the levels of a factor.

tgs_matrix_tapply(x, index, fun, ..., margin = 2)

Arguments

x

a matrix or a sparse matrix of 'dgCMatrix' type

index

a factor (or a vector, coerced to a factor by 'as.factor') of the same length as the number of columns of 'x' (or rows, if 'margin' is 1)

fun

the function to be applied

...

optional arguments to 'fun'

margin

2 (the default) to group the columns of 'x' by 'index', 1 to group the rows. Can only be passed by name.

Value

A matrix with a row for each level of 'index' and a column for each row of 'x' (or column, if 'margin' is 1). The [i, j] element is the result of applying 'fun' to x[j, index == levels(index)[i]] (or to x[index == levels(index)[i], j] if 'margin' is 1), and NA for a level of 'index' that has no values.
Note that the return value is a dense matrix even when x is sparse.

Details

'tgs_matrix_tapply(x, index, fun)' is essentialy an efficient implementation of 'apply(mat, 1, function(x) tapply(x, index, fun))'. 'tgs_matrix_tapply(x, index, fun, margin = 1)' groups the rows instead of the columns: it is the same as 'tgs_matrix_tapply(t(x), index, fun)' without transposing 'x', and for 'sum' the same as 'rowsum(x, index)'.

'sum', 'mean', 'max', 'min' and 'median' are computed in C++ when 'fun' is passed by name (e.g. 'fun = max', not 'fun = function(v) max(v)') and the only other argument is 'na.rm' (for 'sum' also the extra values to add, for 'mean' also 'trim = 0'). Any other function is called from R once for every group and row (or column), which is much slower.

The implicit zeros of a sparse matrix are values like any other, e.g. for 'mean', 'median', 'max' and 'min'.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Note: all the available CPU cores might be used

set.seed(seed = 1)
nr <- 6
nc <- 10
mat <- matrix(sample(c(rep(0, 6), 1:3), nr * nc, replace = TRUE), nrow = nr, ncol = nc)
index <- factor(rep_len(1:3, ncol(mat)), levels = 0:5)
r1 <- apply(mat, 1, function(x) tapply(x, index, sum))
r2 <- tgs_matrix_tapply(mat, index, sum)
r3 <- tgs_matrix_tapply(t(mat), index, max, margin = 1)
# }
